messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer 'Gridlytics' reported they didn't receive alerts for a job failure 6161616890 -> looks like our paging didn't fire. I see an engine error in the incident-broker logs.
incubot: [system] incoming page for escalation_id=esc-9ab2 queued, applying suppressor rules. result=SUPPRESSED (dedupe-key=dedup:esc-9ab2)
oncall-sam: Noted, i'm oncall. Alex, can you paste the incident id and any logs?
alex: incident id=ingest:job-4721, earliest failure 6161616890, customer ticket #1543. Logs attached: `ERROR: checkpoint upload timeout`
priya: I'm seeing the same on the alert-relay logs — a flurry of duplicate retries, incubot picks up and marks as dedupe. but pager didn't go out.
sre-liz: can someone run a quick TTL check on the suppressor cache (redis)? I've seen TTL drift on the HA failover before.
alex: running: ```redis-cli -h redis-1 GET dedup:esc-9ab2``` -> "esc-9ab2:6161616890"
alex: then ```redis-cli -h redis-1 TTL dedup:esc-9ab2``` -> `-1`
sre-liz: TTL -1 means the key is persistent. That explains dedupe blocking repeated pages. Any recent config push to make keys persistent?
priya: we rotated redis replicas in the last deploy (6161616400) to promote failover, iirc we forgot to reapply expiry script on the new master.
oncall-sam: so incubot saw the dedupe key and suppressed, but the key never expired. customers primary alerts were suppressed as duplicates. What's the customer impact window?
alex: Gridlytics missed 3 pages between 6161616890 and 6161617100. They called support at 6161617130. Engineering alert for job pipeline tied to that page was suppressed.
sre-liz: mitigation plan: 1) delete stale dedupe keys for affected window 2) re-enable expiry policy on redis 3) temporarily suspend dedupe suppressor for critical integrations while we confirm. Any objections?
priya: agree. I'll run a targeted delete for keys matching `dedup:esc-*6161616*` and reenable the expiry cron.
oncall-sam: please also trigger manual pages for the missed esc-ids and notify Gridlytics we are paging them now and investigating. I'll take manual paging.
alex: running delete: ```redis-cli -h redis-1 KEYS "dedup:esc-*6161616*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis-1 DEL``` -> deleted 42 keys
alex: reapplying expiry helper: ```/usr/local/bin/dedupe-expirer --bind redis-1 --ttl 300 --daemonize``` -> started
incubot: [system] suppressor disabled for channel=critical-integrations by admin=true (temporary)
oncall-sam: manual page sent to Gridlytics at 6161617220 via SMS and call bridge. They confirmed receipt. marking customer-impact=yes
sre-liz: monitoring: setting a one-off alert to watch for `dedupe key persist` and increase visibility on redis TTLs. Also creating an automatic rollback to re-enable suppressor after verification.
priya: added a runbook step to the incident-bot config: if redis master age > 5m after failover, run expiry-reapply. filing PR to add to infra-deploy scripts.
alex: customer comms: advise they had delayed alerts ~> ~35m between 6161616890 and 6161617100. ops already opened ticket and informed CS.
oncall-sam: open to the group: should we keep suppressor off for 30m to ensure no more false dedupes? I'm leaning yes while we validate.
sre-liz: ok to keep suppressed for 20m only, then auto re-enable. we don't want to create duplicates if there really are floods. set conservative window.
priya: implemented TTL watch and temporary window: incubot will remain in 'bypass-dedupe' mode until 6161618345 or until manual re-enable.
incubot: [system] bypass-dedupe=true until 6161618345; logging all suppressed->bypassed decisions
alex: notes for postmortem: root cause = expiry cron not reattached after redis master promotion; contributing factor = suppressor trusts dedupe keys without TTL sanity checks; mitigation = targeted key delete, reattach expiry, add TTL sanity checks in incubot, add runbook and telemetry.
oncall-sam: customer impact = delayed alerts to Gridlytics (one customer) for ~35 minutes; no known production data loss.
sre-liz: next steps: create a postmortem doc, link runbook, track infra PR (pri-432) and incubot change (inc-789) to add TTL fallback (if TTL == -1 and key age > X then treat as expired).
priya: i'm on the PRs. alex can you open the postmortem and include timeline + commands?
alex: will open the postmortem and ping the CS thread with customer comms draft.
incubot: [system] note: incident automation logged 8 suppressed messages that were bypassed during manual window.
priya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with infra to ensure failover docs updated. :thumbsup:
oncall-sam: thanks — i'll stay on watch until 6161617400 then handoff to the next oncall. :phone:
sre-liz: ack. moving to monitoring and closure checklist.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rolled back toaster-service v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 at 6161617350 (not related but FYI)
alex: closing thread for live coord; will update postmortem link when created.
